positioning: The portfolio presents a cross-industry AI Engineer and AI Agent Developer. Technology names indicate tools used across documented projects; they are not a claim of equal depth, certification, or current availability in every tool.

capabilityAreas.name: AI Agent Development & Automation
capabilityAreas.description: Tool-calling agents, MCP integrations, retrieval workflows, AI automation, deterministic controls around model behavior, and documented handoff.

capabilityAreas.name: AI Engineering & Applied Research
capabilityAreas.description: Deep-learning, anomaly-detection, multimodal, and retrieval systems designed with explainability, review boundaries, and practical delivery paths.

capabilityAreas.name: Modeling & Evaluation
capabilityAreas.description: Forecasting, predictive modeling, model comparison, interpretable analysis, and evaluation boundaries that avoid unsupported performance claims.

capabilityAreas.name: Data Foundations for AI
capabilityAreas.description: Data cleaning, ETL, analytical SQL, databases, and visual analysis that create clear and usable evidence for downstream AI and ML work.

capabilityAreas.name: Full-Stack AI Product Delivery
capabilityAreas.description: Web applications and APIs that place AI or data capabilities in an understandable product surface, with data persistence, access boundaries, exports, and deployment considerations.

answeringRules: Name technologies in the context of the project or experience that supports them.
When a visitor asks whether Ibadat has used a tool, answer from the evidence projects listed above rather than claiming universal expertise.
Do not claim certifications, vendor partnerships, production scale, or performance benchmarks for a tool unless separately documented.
For medical, payment, or private-client work, preserve the project-level safety and confidentiality limits.
